images.title: From number cases to one identity
images.purpose: Shows the identity tool's core move: three number cases of a pattern become one statement with letters, which also passes a test with a negative number and a fraction.
images.composition: Three small cards stacked on the left, one grey arrow, one large card on the right, and one small test card below the large card. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: Left: three equal white cards with thin dark outlines, stacked vertically, reading '9² − 1² = 10 × 8', '5² − 2² = 7 × 3' and '5² − 1² = 6 × 4'. A grey (#6B7280) arrow points right to one larger card with a teal (#0072B2) outline reading 'a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)'. Below that card, a smaller card with a reddish purple (#CC79A7) outline reading 'a = −3, b = 1/2' and under it '8.75 = 8.75'. Exactly 5 cards and 1 arrow.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: Written with letters, a pattern holds for every number, negatives and fractions too.
images.description: Shows the identity tool's core move: three number cases of a pattern become one statement with letters, which also passes a test with a negative number and a fraction.

image_decisions.why: The practice tests whether patterns hold beyond counting numbers; the card picture shows the generalising move.
